name: Barcelona
description: Vibrant coastal city on the Mediterranean, known for Gaudí architecture, urban beaches, and rich Catalan culture.

name: Sitges
description: Seaside town southwest of Barcelona famous for its beaches, LGBTQ+ friendly scene, and film festival.

name: Tarragona
description: Historic port city on Spain’s Costa Daurada, featuring Roman ruins, a cathedral, and golden beaches.

name: Montserrat
description: Mountainous monastery complex northwest of Barcelona, known for its unique rock formations and hiking trails.

name: Valencia
description: Spain’s third-largest city, blending futuristic architecture and historical charm, with famous paella and beaches.

name: Albufera Natural Park
description: Wetland nature reserve south of Valencia, home to rice paddies, birdlife, and traditional fishing villages.

name: Xàtiva
description: Historic inland town famous for its medieval castle and scenic hilltop views over the Vall d’Albaida.

name: Alicante
description: Lively port city on Spain’s Costa Blanca with a castle overlooking the sea, old town nightlife, and long beaches.

name: Benidorm
description: High-rise resort city on the Costa Blanca known for its beaches, nightlife, and holiday atmosphere.

name: Calpe
description: Coastal town north of Alicante, dominated by the Peñón de Ifach rock and known for seafood restaurants.

name: Dénia
description: Harbor town halfway between Alicante and Valencia, with ferry connections to Ibiza and a local castle.

name: Jávea
description: Charming seaside town with coves, cliffs, and turquoise waters popular with divers and expats.

name: Elche
description: UNESCO-listed palm grove city near Alicante, known for its historic center and palm-tree-filled landscapes.

name: Torrevieja
description: Coastal town south of Alicante known for its pink salt lagoons, beaches, and relaxed Mediterranean vibe.

name: Castellón de la Plana
description: Lesser-known coastal city north of Valencia, offering authentic Spanish culture and long sandy beaches.

name: Peñíscola
description: Walled medieval town on the Costa del Azahar, set on a rocky headland with a seaside castle.

name: Altea
description: Whitewashed coastal village north of Benidorm, famous for its blue-domed church and artistic vibe.

name: Cádiz
description: Ancient port city surrounded by the Atlantic Ocean, known for its old town charm, golden beaches, and lively Andalusian culture.

name: Jerez de la Frontera
description: Cultural hub famous for sherry wine, Andalusian horses, and flamenco traditions, located inland from Cádiz.

name: Tarifa
description: Europe’s southernmost town where the Mediterranean meets the Atlantic, popular for kitesurfing and bohemian beach vibes.

name: Vejer de la Frontera
description: Whitewashed hilltop village overlooking the Atlantic, offering narrow streets, artisan shops, and sunset views.

name: Conil de la Frontera
description: Relaxed seaside town with wide sandy beaches, surf spots, and a laid-back Andalusian feel.

name: Zahara de los Atunes
description: Unspoiled coastal village known for its pristine beaches, tuna gastronomy, and tranquil charm.

name: El Palmar
description: Rustic beach destination near Vejer, loved by surfers and digital nomads for its sunsets and chiringuitos.

name: Sanlúcar de Barrameda
description: Historic coastal town at the Guadalquivir River mouth, famous for manzanilla sherry and seafood on Bajo de Guía beach.

name: El Puerto de Santa María
description: Elegant port city across the bay from Cádiz, known for sherry bodegas, sailing, and fine beaches.

name: Rota
description: Beach town north of Cádiz with calm waters, family-friendly resorts, and traditional Andalusian atmosphere.

name: Chipiona
description: Coastal town famous for its lighthouse, moscatel wine, and beaches stretching toward the Guadalquivir River.

name: Madrid
description: Spain's capital, a high-energy city of grand boulevards, world-class museums, and late-night tapas culture.

name: Seville
description: Andalusian capital with flamenco roots, a Moorish-Gothic cathedral, and the lush Alcázar gardens.

name: Granada
description: Sierra Nevada–set city crowned by the Alhambra and famous for free-tapas bars and Albaicín views.

name: Córdoba
description: Andalusian city famed for the UNESCO-listed Mezquita-Catedral and flower-filled patios in the Judería.

name: Málaga
description: Costa del Sol gateway with Picasso's birthplace, an emerging art scene, and tapas-rich old town.

name: Marbella
description: Costa del Sol resort town synonymous with luxury marinas, Puerto Banús nightlife, and elegant old quarter.

name: Ronda
description: Cliff-perched white town split by a 100-metre gorge and one of the oldest bullrings in Spain.

name: Mijas
description: Whitewashed mountain village above the Costa del Sol with steep cobbled streets and panoramic Mediterranean views.

name: Nerja
description: East-Costa-del-Sol town built around the 'Balcón de Europa' cliff and the prehistoric Nerja Caves.

name: Bilbao
description: Industrial city reborn around the Guggenheim, Basque pintxos bars, and a riverside art scene.

name: San Sebastián
description: Belle-Époque seaside city famed for La Concha bay, Michelin-density gastronomy, and pintxos crawls.

name: Santander
description: Cantabrian capital wrapped around a deep bay, with grand promenades and Magdalena palace beaches.

name: Oviedo
description: Asturian capital celebrated for its medieval old town, cider houses, and pre-Romanesque churches.

name: Gijón
description: Asturian coast city with surf-friendly San Lorenzo beach and a lively cider-house old quarter.

name: Toledo
description: UNESCO-listed 'City of Three Cultures' on a hilltop loop of the Tagus, with Christian, Jewish, and Moorish quarters.

name: Segovia
description: UNESCO Castilian city defined by a Roman aqueduct, fairytale Alcázar, and famous roast suckling pig.

name: Salamanca
description: Honey-stoned UNESCO city centred on Plaza Mayor and one of Europe's oldest universities.

name: Ávila
description: High-altitude walled city encircled by intact medieval ramparts and tied to Saint Teresa.

name: Cuenca
description: UNESCO Castilian town clinging to a gorge, famed for the 'casas colgadas' hanging houses.

name: Zaragoza
description: Halfway between Madrid and Barcelona, an Ebro-side city of Mudéjar churches and the Pilar basilica.

name: Pamplona
description: Navarran city wrapped in star-shaped citadel walls, famous for the San Fermín running of the bulls.

name: Logroño
description: Rioja capital with a compact tapas alley (Calle Laurel) and rolling vineyards on the doorstep.

name: Santiago de Compostela
description: Galician pilgrimage city and UNESCO old town crowned by the cathedral that ends the Camino de Santiago.

name: A Coruña
description: Atlantic Galician city wrapped around a glass-galleried promenade and the Roman 'Tower of Hercules'.

name: Palma de Mallorca
description: Capital of Mallorca: Gothic cathedral on the bay, a maze of medieval lanes, and turquoise calas nearby.

name: Sóller
description: Mallorcan valley town surrounded by orange groves and linked to its port by a vintage wooden tram.

name: Mahón
description: Menorca's capital wrapped around one of the deepest natural harbours in the Mediterranean.

name: Ibiza Town
description: UNESCO Dalt Vila citadel above a marina that doubles as the Mediterranean nightlife capital.

name: Formentera
description: Tiny Balearic island known for almost-Caribbean turquoise water and dune-backed beaches.

name: Santa Cruz de Tenerife
description: Tenerife's capital, a port city with the wave-shaped Auditorio and the dark-sand Las Teresitas beach nearby.

name: Teide National Park
description: Spain's tallest peak rising from a Mars-like volcanic caldera, a UNESCO park ringed with hiking trails.

name: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria
description: Year-round-warm Canary capital with the long urban beach of Las Canteras and a lively colonial old town.

name: Arrecife
description: Lanzarote's capital, gateway to volcanic landscapes and César Manrique's signature architectural sites.
